\[
T = m + k\, s,
\quad
I_{\text{out}} = \begin{cases} 255 & I > T \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases},
\qquad k = -0.2
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(m, s\): The local mean and standard deviation
- \(k\): The weight of the deviation

m and s are the mean and the population standard deviation of the window around the pixel. Niblack sets the threshold at m + k s, with k = -0.2 for dark text on a light page. The deviation adapts the threshold to the local contrast. scikit-image's threshold_niblack writes it as m - k s, so its k has the opposite sign. The result is 255 where the value is above the threshold and 0 elsewhere, or the reverse with Invert.
